- When sentiment is positive (≥0.5) and forecast shows strong upward bias, reduce peak forecasts by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.0) and forecast is rising, cap upward momentum early — model tends to overreact to negative sentiment.  
- After a recent spike in price, model often overcorrects downward — apply a 3–5 day lagged mean reversion buffer to prevent premature drop.  
- When sentiment is neutral (0.0–0.25) and forecast is trending, reduce forecast slope by 10–15% to avoid false momentum.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion within 5–7 days after a peak, model tends to overpredict continuation — adjust forecast to align with 3–5 day moving average.  
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, if sentiment is volatile or mixed, reduce forecast variance — model overfits to short-term sentiment noise.
